transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-23
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan, Priya, Evan (Redwood) — Aisha, Michael, Greg, Sofia, Tom (Tessera)
Links referenced: pilot-deck-v2.pdf, capacity-map.xlsx, SECURITY-SOC2-2026.pdf (shared in chat)

Summary:
- Tessera needs a 6-week pilot to validate cost/latency tradeoffs for product search and personalization features.
- Primary tension: latency SLA for user-facing search (p95 < 120ms) vs unit cost targets from FinOps.
- Security requires VPC private deployment with KMS integration; SOC2 evidence requested.
- Agreed next steps: Redwood to send pricing options and capacity BOM; Priya to produce traces and batching guidance; schedule kickoff for early June.

Topics:
- Pilot success criteria and timeline
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment constraints
- Cost modeling and batching/kv-cache suggestions
- Security controls: SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs, data residency
- SLA negotiation and fallback policies

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Kim: Alright everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have a pretty full agenda — we'll try to keep this to under an hour. Quick intros?
[00:08] Aisha Rahman: Hi I'm Aisha, VP Eng at Tessera, we run the search and rec infra, looking to push inference into prod for personalization.
[00:13] Michael Soto: Michael, Head of ML. we'll be owning model eval and the pilot.
[00:17] Greg Ortiz: Greg, FinOps, i'll be very direct about cost targets.
[00:20] Sofia Liu: Sofia, security, will need SOC2 bit and network details.
[00:24] Jordan Kim: Great, thanks. Priya and Evan from our side — Priya will walk some technical tradeoffs, Evan will own onboarding and trial ops.
[00:31] Priya Patel: Hey all. I'll start with a quick recap of what we saw in your pre-call perf traces and then propose a pilot matrix. There were some noisy tails in the p95 for longer contexts.
[00:41] Tom Becker: Sorry quick interject: we're mostly concerned about user-facing search latency; we can't have >150ms p95 for query completions.
[00:48] Priya Patel: Totally, Tom. For a user-facing search route we typically recommend either Dedicated or Private with prefix caching enabled — hosted can work but you'd see higher variance under burst.
[00:58] Michael Soto: On the model side, our average prompt length is ~120 tokens, but recs can go up to 600 when we include full session history, so we need KV cache behavior to avoid linear re-compute.
[01:12] Priya Patel: Ok that's helpful. We can enable autoregressive KV cache plus prefix caching; that should reduce token computation for repeated context. I'll attach a configuration that shows hit-rate assumptions.
[01:23] Greg Ortiz: Cost-wise, our target is about 30% lower unit cost than ModelCo Cloud. Can Redwood get us there with quantization and batching?
[01:31] Jordan Kim: Short answer: yes, for many workloads. We typically combine T4 or A10-based Dedicated pools with int8 quantization profiles and workload-aware batching. The Optimize toolkit will give suggestions automatically after sample traces.
[01:43] Priya Patel: If you can accept slightly higher tail latency on cold starts, batching can drop unit cost significantly — up to 40% in our internal tests for similar traffic patterns. But it requires predictable concurrency or a small scheduler buffer.
[01:56] Michael Soto: We need that tradeoff quantified. Can you run a simulated batch-run with our traces?
[02:01] Priya Patel: Yes, send the traces, I'll run the simulation. I'll include per-route batch size recommendations and expected p95 impact.
[02:07] Aisha Rahman: On SLA — our product team wants p95 < 120ms for search, but we can be flexible if you provide automatic fallback to a cheaper, lower-capacity model when under stress.
[02:19] Jordan Kim: That's a reasonable ask. Our runtime supports smart routing and fallbacks — you can pin routes and have an automatic fallback to a quantized variant. That will preserve availability even if the high-capacity pool saturates. We can include that in the pilot scope.
[02:34] Sofia Liu: From security, we require: VPC peering or Private deployment, KMS integration for key management, retention policy configurable per-route, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. SOC2 documents are required as part of procurement.
[02:48] Evan Cho: We can provide a Private deployment that sits in your VPC and integrates with your KMS/HSM. We also have a secure control-plane option if you need customer-managed networking. I'll share our network diagram.
[02:59] Sofia Liu: Also SSO via SAML, RBAC scoped to teams, and the ability to redact PII in logs — can you support that?
[03:07] Jordan Kim: Yes on SAML and RBAC. For PII redaction we have options: token-level masking and a log redaction pipeline. We'll note that as requirements for the pilot.
[03:18] Tom Becker: A quick infra note — our infra team prefers minimal outbound connectivity from the model hosts; do you need any egress for model updates?
[03:26] Evan Cho: For Private deployments you can block outbound except to our control-plane endpoints; we can also provide an air-gapped option for offline model packaging, but that adds operational overhead.
[03:36] Greg Ortiz: Budget ask — roughly what's the minimum monthly commit to get Dedicated pools?
[03:41] Jordan Kim: Our Dedicated starter size is X vGPU units — for your expected peak (from the capacity map you shared) you'd land in the mid-tier reserved capacity. I'll include concrete numbers in the BOM.
[03:52] Aisha Rahman: We need a pilot that proves two things: 1) that we can meet p95 latency under typical traffic, and 2) that cost per query with batching/quantization is within 20% of our current target.
[04:05] Priya Patel: Proposed pilot matrix: two-week baseline on hosted (to get traces), three-week Dedicated/Private pilot to test p95 and KV cache, one week of stress/scale testing with fallbacks. Total ~6 weeks.
[04:18] Michael Soto: That ordering makes sense. We want to include a canary for model rollouts too.
[04:23] Priya Patel: We'll include canary/deploy policy — canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% with rollback triggers on quality or latency regressions.
[04:33] Jordan Kim: Ok let's discuss the specific measurements and dashboards. We'll provide per-route token cost, p50/p95/p99, batching utilization, cache hit rate, and a regression alert hooked to your eval suite.
[04:44] Tom Becker: For monitoring and alerts, do we need to send traces to your console or can we integrate with Datadog?
[04:50] Evan Cho: Both. We push verbose traces to Redwood Console but you can forward metrics and traces to Datadog/Prometheus; we include tracing hooks.
[04:59] Sofia Liu: About compliance docs — can you provide evidence for SOC2, ISO, and your pen-test schedule? Also indicate whether Redwood supports our KMS vendor (HashiCorp Vault + AWS KMS).
[05:12] Jordan Kim: Yes, SOC2 package is available, ISO is in scope, pen-test summary we can provide. We integrate with HashiCorp Vault and AWS KMS; the Private deployment supports customer-managed keys.
[05:24] Greg Ortiz: Are there any upfront engineering investments from our side for the Private deployment? What's the timeline to stand up a VPC connected instance?
[05:31] Evan Cho: Typically 2-3 weeks for initial provisioning and security review, assuming access to your networking team. The air-gapped option is longer.
[05:37] Michael Soto: During the Dedicated pilot can we run a side-by-side compare to ModelCo Cloud? We want apples-to-apples latency and cost numbers.
[05:45] Priya Patel: Yes, we'll provide the same request traces and a controlled experiment. Provide the credentials and we'll run the tests; we'll deliver a benchmark report.
[05:53] Aisha Rahman: One concern — ModelCo offered a credit for migration. Will Redwood match on pricing or provide any migration support?
[06:00] Jordan Kim: We can discuss pilot credits and migration assistance. For migration support we provide a technical migration SKU and an onboarding services package. I'll include details.
[06:11] Greg Ortiz: Ok good. Any risks we should call out?
[06:14] Priya Patel: Biggest risk is model context size causing cache thrash if session keys are not normalized — that increases token compute. Suggest canonicalizing session context and using shorter summaries to keep prompt length stable.
[06:27] Michael Soto: We'll prototype that in the baseline weeks.
[06:31] Evan Cho: Another risk is burst concurrency — autoscaling limits and queueing can spike p95; we'll outline autoscale baselines and burst policies in the BOM.
[06:40] Tom Becker: From infra, fine, but we need explicit egress rules and a hard list of IPs.
[06:46] Evan Cho: We'll provide that list and a network diagram.
[06:50] Jordan Kim: Great. To recap — action items and timeline: Jordan sends pricing/BOM; Priya runs batch simulations and shares traces; Evan prepares onboarding doc and network diagram; Sofia will send compliance checklist. Pilot kickoff tentatively 2026-06-08.
[07:05] Aisha Rahman: That works for us, pending pricing and compliance signoff.
[07:09] Jordan Kim: Perfect. Any final questions?
[07:11] Greg Ortiz: One more: can you provide a sample contract clause for SLA and credits?
[07:16] Jordan Kim: We'll send a proposed SLA appendix and credit table with the pricing doc.
[07:21] Sofia Liu: And please ensure PIIs in logs are redacted before forwarding to our SIEM in the pilot.
[07:26] Evan Cho: Noted, we'll include log-redaction config.
[07:29] Michael Soto: Thanks everyone — let's follow up in the chat and confirm the kickoff.
[07:33] Jordan Kim: Thanks all.

End of transcript.
notes: Pilot emphasis on latency-cost tradeoff and Private deployment constraints; Tessera requires SOC2 + KMS; target kickoff early June.
